stem:
Bacteria can be classified according to the type of cell wall they have.

Gram-negative bacteria have a cell wall with an outer layer known as the outer membrane.

Gram-positive bacteria do not have an outer membrane, but have a much thicker peptidoglycan layer than Gram-negative bacteria.

Fig. 4.1 is a diagram of a section through the cell wall of a **Gram-negative** bacterium.
{{figure:figure_4_1.webp}}
